candidates.name: HotelRec
candidates.what_it_holds: ~50M hotel reviews scraped from TripAdvisor (global coverage, sample rows show data from 2010 onward), released with Antognini & Faltings LREC 2020 paper 'HotelRec: a Novel Very Large-Scale Hotel Recommendation Dataset'. Fields per review: hotel URL, reviewer profile URL, date, overall rating, title, full text, and sub-ratings (cleanliness, service, value, etc). Actual data download requires filling a separate access-request form; license restricted to academic research only. 17 commits on GitHub repo (metadata/scripts/paper only, not the raw reviews).
candidates.why_useful: TripAdvisor review-volume-and-rating time series across a huge global hotel panel is a competitor/adjacent-supply engagement proxy (gap #9, and loosely gap #5 engagement signals) analogous to how Inside Airbnb reviews are used as a stays-index kernel for ABNB nights; review dates could be aggregated into a monthly hotel-demand pulse by market if the gated download is obtained.
candidates.size_hint: ~50M reviews, largest hotel-review dataset publicly documented
candidates.time_coverage: ~2010–2020 (per paper), TripAdvisor reviews accumulate historically further back per hotel
candidates.last_activity: 17 commits, repo tied to a 2020 LREC paper (exact last-commit date not visible without deeper history)

candidates.name: TidyTuesday Hotel Bookings (2020-02-11)
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed CSVs (hotels.csv combined, plus H1.csv resort / H2.csv city variants in some mirrors) — the Antonio, Almeida & Nunes (2019, Data in Brief) Portugal hotel-booking dataset, ~119,390 rows total across a resort hotel (H1, Algarve) and a city hotel (H2, Lisbon), Jul 2015–Aug 2017, 32 columns incl. lead time, cancellation flag, ADR, deposit type, market segment, booking channel, special requests.
candidates.why_useful: Well-packaged, clean, well-documented mirror of the exact dataset CONTEXT.md already lists as held (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes) — not new, but flagged per instructions as a duplicate worth one line since it is a clean canonical copy with column dictionary and is the base every other 'successor' repo in this space re-uses.
candidates.geography: Portugal (Algarve resort hotel + Lisbon city hotel)
candidates.license: CC0 (tidytuesday convention) / original CC-BY 4.0 from Data in Brief
candidates.last_activity: Static historical tidytuesday week, repo itself active
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Portugal hotel-booking demand dataset (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes) — already held per CONTEXT.md

candidates.name: INN Hotels Group Reservations (ahsan81 Kaggle mirror)
candidates.what_it_holds: 36,275 reservation rows, 19 features, for an unnamed Indian hotel chain ('INN Hotels Group') sourced originally from Kaggle (ahsan81/hotel-reservations-classification-dataset). Fields include lead time, arrival date, number of adults/children, weekend/week nights, meal plan, room type, market segment, average price per room, special requests, and booking-status (cancelled/not-cancelled) target — CSV format, MIT-style permissive Kaggle mirror, 57,080 Kaggle downloads per HF card. Not on GitHub itself (found via Hugging Face's dataset API since GitHub/web search engines were rate-limited or blocked this session); several other HF mirrors of the same underlying Kaggle set also exist (Omrihahami/HotelReservationsDataset, sanjula153/Hotel-Reservation-Dataset, Brbg/Hotel_Reservation).
candidates.why_useful: A second, independent (non-Portugal, non-Antonio) real-world PMS-style reservation dataset with lead time and cancellation status — useful as an out-of-sample cross-check for any cancellation/lead-time model built on the Antonio data, and it is India-geography which none of our held hotel datasets cover.
candidates.time_coverage: Not stated in card (Kaggle upload ~2022, underlying stay dates unspecified)

candidates.name: Mindweave Synthetic Hotel PMS Dataset
candidates.what_it_holds: Synthetic, relationally-consistent PMS dataset generated by Mindweave Technologies: 4 tables (guests, properties, rooms, reservations). Free sample 2,180 rows; full dataset 21,808 rows (8,000 guests, 3 properties, 177 rooms, 13,628 reservations) sold via Gumroad, CC-BY-NC-4.0. Includes seasonal pricing that fluctuates with demand, lead time and cancellation patterns with 'realistic' distributions, and injected anomalies (a March conference booking surge, a November facility closure). Available as CSV/Parquet/SQLite. Not on GitHub; no linked source repo.
candidates.why_useful: A structurally realistic multi-table PMS schema (guests/rooms/properties/reservations) that could serve as a template for what a real STR/hotel PMS export looks like, useful mainly as a methods reference rather than as ABNB-relevant real data; low direct value since it is synthetic and partly paywalled.
candidates.size_hint: 21,808 reservation rows across 4 tables (2,180-row free sample)
candidates.license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (free sample); full dataset commercial via Gumroad

candidates.name: RMOL (Revenue Management Open Library)
candidates.what_it_holds: C++ open-source revenue-management simulation library (part of the airsim/travel-market-simulator suite alongside stdair, airinv, tvlsim). Implements classic RM optimisation (EMSR, nesting, forecasting of booking curves) originally built for airline seat inventory but generically applicable to any capacity/date-based booking-curve RM problem, including hotel rooms. No committed real-world hotel data; it is a simulator/library, not a dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Could be used to synthesize realistic booking-curve / lead-time / cancellation-and-no-show test data under controllable demand assumptions as a kernel analogue for RNPL/booking-pace modeling (gap #17 methods, gap #18 book-ahead analogues), though it requires nontrivial setup and produces simulated, not observed, data.
candidates.license: Open source (LGPL per airsim project convention)
candidates.last_activity: Low-activity legacy academic project (airsim org, 14 stars)

candidates.name: Hotel Cancellation Minimization & Booking Behavior Analysis
candidates.what_it_holds: Analysis project (SQL + Python + Power BI .pbix) over the same Antonio/Almeida/Nunes-style two-Portugal-property dataset (Lisbon city hotel + Algarve resort hotel, ~100k+ raw records, 86,113 bookings in the final analysed set, Jul 2015–Oct 2017) with cancellation-status, advance-booking-window (lead time), ADR, and booking-channel (TA/TO, Corporate, Direct, GDS) fields. Raw CSV not clearly committed in-repo (analysis outputs and BI file are); described as sourced from Kaggle/ScienceDirect.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms channel-segmented lead-time and cancellation breakdowns (TA/TO vs Corporate vs Direct vs GDS) on the already-held Antonio data that our own construction may not have replicated; low incremental value as it is a duplicate source, but the channel segmentation could be a useful reference for gap #3 (booking lead time / cancellation-rate distributions).
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: Portugal hotel-booking demand dataset (Antonio/Almeida/Nunes) — already held per CONTEXT.md

notes: This theme's web-search modality hit unusually severe tooling failures this session: WebSearch had already exhausted its 200-call session budget before I could run a single query (likely consumed by earlier scouts in this sweep). Every fallback search engine tried via WebFetch either CAPTCHA-blocked (DuckDuckGo standard and lite), 403'd (Ecosia, Mojeek), 429'd (Brave Search, github.com/search — Retry-After 3600s, consistent with many concurrent scouts hitting it despite the no-gh-CLI rule not covering the website), or returned generic non-filtered results that ignored the site: operator and query terms entirely (Bing, Google, Marginalia) — these engines appear to serve a cached/generic SERP to the WebFetch summarizer rather than real query-specific results, so 'no results' from them should not be read as 'nothing exists', just as 'this route did not work this session'. The one reliable route was Hugging Face's public JSON dataset-search API (huggingface.co/api/datasets?search=...), which is not GitHub but surfaced real, verifiable dataset mirrors and confirmed that essentially all Kaggle-mirrored 'hotel booking'/'hotel reservation' datasets circulating (SIEP, jason1966/ahsan81, Omrihahami, sanjula153, Brbg) trace back to either the already-held Antonio/Almeida/Nunes Portugal set or the India-based INN Hotels Group set — I did not find evidence of a genuine third independent large real-world hotel-PMS dataset, nor of an extended/longer/more-recent successor to Antonio et al. covering more years or more properties. GitHub topic pages (topics/hotel-booking, /revenue-management, /hotel-reservation) worked without rate-limiting and were exhaustively checked — they are dominated by hotel-booking *application* software (WordPress plugins, MERN/React booking-system CRUD apps, PMS UI clones like qloapps) with essentially no committed real datasets; the one RM-adjacent tooling hit (airsim/rmol) is airline, not hotel, and simulation-only. Recommendation for whoever re-runs this theme: retry with a working `gh search repos`/`gh api search/code` pass once the github.com/search rate limit clears (~1hr from now), since that is likely to surface far more than what browser-side search allowed this session; also worth trying Kaggle's own search API directly (kaggle.com/api or the dataset-search JSON) for a broader Portugal/India-adjacent hotel PMS dataset census, and checking Mendeley Data directly for the original Antonio et al. deposit page (may list newer related deposits by the same authors).
